T14_architecture.note: The architecture is a conceptual proposal informed by the charted evidence; it was not coded in the corpus, and no included study tests it. Basis states where each element comes from: the coded studies (corpus), a gap in the coded studies (corpus gap), the monitoring reviews {Pereira2025}, {DiDomenico2026}, {Pereira2026}, {Cosme2025}, IEC 61724-1 {IEC61724}, or design reasoning. The decision timescale is the interval at which a decision is revised. Each data list is split into what standard PV monitoring already provides (IEC 61724-1), the minimum addition proposed for a digital shadow of that function, and research-grade items for pilot installations. Tiers follow the latency each function tolerates and a footprint criterion: each function runs at the lowest tier that meets its latency, so remote (cloud) computing is limited to seasonal planning and retraining (F4-F5 re-planning, F6 cleaning planning, F7, F8), which run a few times per season and keep data transfer and remote computing energy small. Row G applies to every tier. Suggested recording intervals: PV and irradiance channels as IEC 61724-1 specifies for its Class A or B systems; PAR and microclimate 1 to 10 minutes; soil moisture 15 to 60 minutes. Sensor counts, accuracy classes, sampling intervals, record lengths, and maintenance intervals are left open; for the PV channels they are set by IEC 61724-1 {IEC61724}. Fallback set-points for loss of data or communication belong to every row executed at the edge; they are discussed with Figure 3.

T15_readiness.caption: Table 15 Readiness by Decision: Full-Text Models That Meet Each Successive Condition of the Strict Rule
header: Every traded-off output validated, with an error statistic
Also links the subsystems in one model
Also validated on data independent of calibration
Also a time step fine enough for the decision (ready)
For comparison: meets the base rule
T15_readiness.note: Full-text core, 208 studies with a virtual model. Each column counts the studies in the previous column that also meet the stated condition, so each row nests; the 'any' row counts studies that meet the conditions for at least one decision. Readiness is judged from the model's capability, whatever decision the study itself addresses. Every traded-off output validated = crop and PV output for tracking and shading control; water and crop for irrigation; PV output and soiling loss for cleaning; each compared with field or laboratory measurements with a reported error statistic. Links the subsystems = one-way or two-way coupling, or a physical feedback represented within one integrated model. Time step fine enough = hourly or finer for tracking, daily or finer for irrigation and cleaning. Base rule = covers the subsystems, at least one decision output validated against any measurements, linked, and of a specific installation (S5, Section Q). No model at any stage is designed to receive installation data automatically (0). A recode of all candidates from the original PDFs, including tables and figures, also found no ready model after adjudication (S2, sheets 'PDF recheck' and 'PDF recheck summary').
